attributes.readMe:
# Offer Letter Template

## Summary
A CardDef holding `name` and a markdown `body` written once and merged many times. The body carries merge placeholders — `{{candidateName}}`, `{{jobTitle}}`, `{{salary}}`, `{{startDate}}`, `{{expiresDate}}`, `{{companyName}}` — the exact vocabulary lives in the exported `MERGE_FIELDS` constant, colocated with the card so the isolated view's legend and the command's interpolation can never drift apart. `title` is computed from `name`; `placeholderTally` is a denormalized computed count of distinct placeholders in the body, which is what the fitted tile reads.

## Import
```ts
import { OfferLetterTemplate, MERGE_FIELDS, placeholdersIn } from './offer-letter-template';
```

## Usage — three or more ways this is used

**1. As GenerateOfferLetterCommand's source document.** The command reads `template.body`, replaces each known placeholder with the linked Offer's real stored values (deterministic string interpolation — deliberately NOT an LLM call, because a letter's salary and dates must be exact), and writes the result to `Offer.letter`. When no template is linked it queries the realm for the first OfferLetterTemplate, so a one-template realm needs no picker.

**2. As the letter-writing surface.** HR edits the body in the card's edit format; the isolated view renders the markdown next to a merge-field legend that marks which fields the body actually uses, so a typo'd token (`{{candidatName}}`) is visible as "not in use" before it ships as literal text in a letter.

**3. As a per-role/per-level variant library.** Multiple templates ("Standard Offer", "Executive Offer", "Contract-to-hire") can coexist; the command's `template` linksTo input picks one explicitly when the realm holds more than the default.

## Template Usage
Isolated: rendered markdown body plus a merge-field legend aside (token, source, in-use highlight). Embedded: icon + name + placeholder count. Fitted: tiered — name → "N merge fields" → a line-clamped plain-text body preview (all own attributes, no link reads). Atom: icon + name.

## Examples
- `OfferLetterTemplate/standard-offer` — the linked example: a realistic standard offer letter using all six merge fields. Run GenerateOfferLetterCommand against any draft/extended Offer to see its merge output land in `Offer.letter` (rendered in the Offer view's letter panel, exported via the print stylesheet).

**Boundary / non-goals:** merge-fields only — no e-signature, no real PDF generation (the Offer isolated view's `@media print` stylesheet is the export path: browser print-to-PDF), no conditional/looping template logic, and no per-candidate template storage (the merged output lives on the Offer, not here).
